title: Polynomial Factorisation
page_title: Polynomial Factorisation | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Maths Revision Notes 2020

blocks.md:
- Factorising a polynomial combines the **factor theorem** with the method of **polynomial division**
- The goal is to break down a polynomial as far as possible into a product of** ***linear factors*

blocks.alt: 2.5.4 Product of linear factors, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.text: How do I factorise a polynomial?

blocks.md: - At A level you will usually be asked to factorise a **cubic** – i.e. a polynomial where the highest power of ***x*** is 3

blocks.alt: 2.5.4 Cubic examples, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - To factorise a cubic polynomial **f(*****x*****)** follow the following steps:

blocks.alt: 2.5.4 Factorisation Illustration_qu, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - Step 1. Find a value*** p*** that makes **f(*****p*****) = **0

blocks.alt: 2.5.4 Factorisation Illustration_1, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - Step 2. Use polynomial division to divide **f(*****x*****) **by **(*****x *****- *****p*****)**

blocks.alt: 2.5.4 Factorisation Illustration_2, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - Step 3. Use the result of your division to write

If the quadratic **(*****ax***<sup>**2**</sup>** + *****bx***** + *****c*****)** is factorisable, factorise it and write **f(*****x*****)** as a product of three linear factors (if the quadratic is not factorisable, then your result from Step 3 is the final factorisation) ![2.5.4 Factorisation Illustration_4, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes](assets/8fc2243e5343-2-5-4-factorisation-illustration-4.png)

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: - The method outlined above can be logically extended to factorise a polynomial of any *degree*.
